verified.analysis: The event is entirely real, contractual, dated and unfired — a signed all-stock acquisition by a named counterparty with a fixed 1.350 ratio, closing expected mid-2027 — so it clears G1 and G2 cleanly. What it does not clear is the capture test: because the consideration is acquirer paper and ON fell 32% since signing (the market punished onsemi for the deal on 2026-06-26, -24% in a day), SYNA has tracked it down 15.8% from the last pre-announcement close, and the residual gap to deal value is only 2.67% gross over ~11 months, roughly cash-equivalent and negative against an assumed ~20% break-downside to a de-rated standalone SYNA. There is no unpriced figure here (G3 fails) and no way for a long-only book to isolate the spread — owning SYNA outright is 1.35x levered exposure to ON's stock, which is a semis macro/direction bet the mandate excludes. GAP: I could not confirm from public filings whether China SAMR clearance is a condition (the announcement cites HSR and "other regulatory approvals" generically); both parties have material China revenue so it is likely, which would only widen timeline risk against an already sub-cash spread. Nothing here to seat.
